# Butler

> Local-first MCP server providing persistent, cross-tool shared memory and
> multi-agent coordination for AI coding agents. State lives in a local
> SQLite event log (`.butler/butler.db`), not inside any single vendor's
> session — so a session in one client (e.g. Claude Code) can hand off to a
> different client (e.g. Kiro CLI, Cursor) with zero lost context.

## What this is for

- An agent (or the user) runs out of usage/credits in one tool and wants to
  resume in another tool without re-explaining the task.
- Multiple agents (same tool or different tools) work the same repo
  concurrently and need to avoid duplicate/conflicting edits.
- A project needs durable TODOs, architectural decisions (ADRs), coding
  rules, and a wiki that persist across IDE reloads and process restarts.
- Multi-step agent orchestration (plan -> implement -> verify -> commit)
  needs shared checkpoint state across stages that may run in different
  tools.

## Transport

MCP server over stdio (JSON-RPC). Install via the `.mcpb` bundle attached to
the latest GitHub Release (https://github.com/Teycir/Butler/releases/latest),
or via `install/install.sh` / `install/install.ps1` which auto-configures
Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Gemini CLI,
Kiro CLI, Kilo Code. No npm package is published; see README.md for the
build-from-source path.

## Core loop for any connecting agent

1. Call `projectlist` (or read `.butler/project.json`) to find/create the
   project id.
2. Call `sessionregister` with a unique `session_id` and your `client_type`.
3. Read resource `butler://projects/{id}/context` to get TODOs, rules,
   decisions, wiki, sessions, and any handoff left by a prior session
   (possibly a different tool).
4. Call `sessionheartbeat` every 15s while active.
5. Before exiting: call `handoffcreate` with a summary, then
   `sessiondisconnect`.

## Tools (19)

Session: `sessionregister`, `sessionheartbeat`, `sessiondisconnect`
Tasks: `todoadd`, `todocomplete`, `todoupdate`, `tododelete`, `todolist`
Coordination: `todoclaim`, `todounclaim`, `messagesend`, `broadcast`, `synccontext`
Knowledge: `wikiupdate`, `ruleadd`, `ruleremove`, `decisionrecord`, `handoffcreate`
Memory: `memorystore`, `memorysearch`, `memorydelete`, `projectlist`
Observability: `eventsexport`, `butlerping`

Full input schemas: see `src/mcp/tools/*.tools.ts` or call each tool's
definition via the MCP `tools/list` method.

## Resources (7)

`butler://projects/{id}/context` (markdown context packet)
`butler://projects/{id}/todos` (JSON)
`butler://projects/{id}/wiki` (JSON)
`butler://projects/{id}/sessions` (JSON)
`butler://projects/{id}/memories` (JSON)
`butler://projects/{id}/diff?since={eventId}` (JSON)
`butler://projects/{id}/orchestration` (LangGraph checkpoints, JSON)

## Machine-readable manifests

- `server.json` — Official MCP Registry manifest (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io),
  namespace `io.github.Teycir/butler`, points at a `.mcpb` bundle attached to
  a GitHub Release (no npm package).
- `manifest.json` — MCPB bundle manifest used to build the `.mcpb` file via
  `npx @anthropic-ai/mcpb pack`.
- `.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` — full server card (tools, resources,
  compatible clients, categories) per SEP-1649.
- `.well-known/mcp.json` — discovery pointer per SEP-1960.
- README.md carries an `<!-- mcp-name: io.github.Teycir/butler -->` marker
  required by the Official MCP Registry's ownership check.

## Docs

- docs/architecture.md — system design detail

- docs/workflows-best-practices.md — recommended agent workflows
- CHANGELOG.md — version history
- skills/butler-workflow/SKILL.md — portable agent skill teaching the core loop above
